headline: Md Zahidul Islam
intro: I build optimization, simulation, and machine-learning models that turn operational requirements and data into decisions. My work spans healthcare scheduling, supply chains, and routing.
availability: Open to Summer 2027 internships in operations research and data science.
interests: My doctoral research connects clinician preferences, fatigue, and operational requirements to better workforce scheduling models. Across my work, I combine mathematical optimization with data analysis and simulation to examine decisions and their trade-offs.
background: I am a Ph.D. candidate at Clemson University. Before Clemson, I pursued graduate research at the University of Tennessee and taught engineering at RUET and Ahsanullah University of Science and Technology in Bangladesh.
community: From student leadership at RUET and the Greater Khulna Association to mentoring undergraduate researchers and leading Clemson’s INFORMS chapter, community involvement has been a continuing part of my academic life.

featured.title: Personalized physician scheduling
featured.description: Translating clinician priorities and hospital requirements into multi-site scheduling models that balance coverage, fairness, and individual preferences.

featured.title: Learning-based routing optimization
featured.alt: Architecture of the learning-based traveling salesman solution method
featured.description: Combining supervised learning with optimization. On 1,000-node instances, published benchmarks showed a 28% smaller average optimality gap and 59% less computation time than a graph pointer network.

featured.title: Supply-chain simulation
featured.description: An agent-based model explores information sharing and risk pooling. Combining both reduced simulated order-to-demand variance by 46.3% at the factory and 49.3% at the wholesaler.
